tagline: Across Saville Dam, with the old town center under the water.
intro: Off US 44, River Road runs north into Pleasant Valley, crosses the West Branch of the Farmington with Route 318, and heads east onto Saville Dam. The road rides the top of it, an embankment 135 feet tall and nearly 2,000 feet long, then comes down to Route 219 along the east shore of Lake McDonough.
Behind the dam lies Barkhamsted Reservoir, Hartford's main water supply. It took until 1948 to fill. Barkhamsted Hollow, the old center of town, went under, and its foundations are still down there.

moments.title: Pleasant Valley
moments.text: The village sits on the west bank of the West Branch, a Wild and Scenic River whose catch-and-release water draws fishermen the year round.

moments.title: Saville Dam
moments.text: Route 318 crosses on top of the dam, which went by Bill's Brook Dam until 1940, when it took the name of the water commission's chief engineer.

moments.title: Lake McDonough
moments.text: Built as the compensating reservoir, to keep the downstream mill owners in water, it now keeps beaches, boats and fishing instead.
